ops.text: The threshold scale near $1\%$ in Eq. (9) presumes a decoder with matching-level accuracy. If the superconducting Baseline is instead decoded by a streaming FPGA decoder that keeps pace with the $1\,\mu$s code cycle, such as Sandpiper [⟦new.A4⟧], whose circuit-level threshold is $0.672\%$, Eq. (9) becomes $p_{L}(p,d)=0.1(p/0.00672)^{(d+1)/2}$. Keeping the expected number of logical failures, $n_{Q}n_{C}\,d\,p_{L}$, below 0.01 as in Eq. (11) for the Fermi-Hubbard benchmark in the Baseline architecture, with $n_{Q}=800$ tiles and $n_{C}=805{,}804$ logical cycles, then requires $d=27$ at $p=10^{-3}$ instead of the $d=23$ listed in Table 7, while at $p=10^{-4}$ the minimum distance stays at $d=11$. The choice of decoder therefore enters the physical-qubit count and the runtime of the distance-scaling architectures through the effective threshold in much the same way as the physical error rate itself.
Dedicated hardware decoders such as Sandpiper [⟦new.A4⟧] can shorten $\tau_{r}$ substantially, although their lower threshold raises the code distance, as estimated in Appendix E.1.
